slides.title: Endocrine System
text: Functions as regulator of multiple body processes

slides.title: Acromegaly
text: Overproduction of growth hormone, after the growth plates are closed
Pt is generally weak and joints which become painful and stiff
Females = amenorrhea, increased facial hair, deep voice
Treatment is removal of Pituitary gland

slides.title: Dwarfism
text: Decrease of growth hormone prior to epiphysis closure

slides.title: Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic
text: Condition that continually releases the antidiuretic hormone (ADH)
Cerebral edema may occur and puts client at risk for seizures
Low urinary output with elevated Sp. gravity
Serum Na level will be decreased because it is diluted
Neuro checks and seizure precautions are implemented
Keep HOB flat or only slightly elevated to decrease the secretion of ADH
IV hypertonic solution if client has hyponatremia

slides.title: Diabetes Insipidus
text: Urine is dilute with low sp.
Polyuria, polydipsia, weakness,    anorectic, loses weight
Vasopressin decreases UOP and increases resorption of water by the renal tubules
Cannot be treated by limiting the intake of fluid, why?

slides.title: A client has Diabetes Insipidus. Which nursing intervention is essential for monitoring this condition?
text: A client has Diabetes Insipidus. Which nursing intervention is essential for monitoring this condition?
Sending a urine specimen to the lab

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client who has syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH).  Which of the following assessment findings would indicate that the client is developing a complication?
text: The nurse is caring for a client who has syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH).  Which of the following assessment findings would indicate that the client is developing a complication?
A weight loss of 3 pounds in 4 days

slides.title: Thyroid Gland
text: These serve as a general pacemaker by accelerating metabolic processes

slides.title: Metabolism: Thyroid Disease
text: Metabolic rate in highly increased due to excessive secretion of thyroid hormones
Antithyroid medication methimazole (Tapazole) blocks the production of thyroid hormones
Iodine is given prior to surgery or in emergencies only
If goiter, cancer, or unresponsive to therapy: thyroidectomy
What medical emergency do we need to monitor for when caring for this client?

slides.title: Metabolism: Thyroid Disease
text: Replacement therapy for the rest of life
Take HR, if over 100 hold and report
What medical emergency do we need to monitor for when caring for this client?

slides.title: Surgical Management of Thyroidectomy
text: Have calcium gluconate at the bedside
Have O2, suction, and trach at bedside
Semi-fowlers position and support the head

slides.title: Parathyroid Glands 4 glands embedded in the back of the thyroid gland
text: Parathyroid Glands 4 glands embedded in the back of the thyroid gland
Give IV calcium gluconate or calcium chloride to bring Calcium level to 7.0
Be careful of IV infiltration because these meds will cause tissue necrosis
Long-term treatment includes oral calcium and Vitamin D supplements

slides.title: Cushing's Disease
text: Overproduction of ACTH as a result of prolonged administration of
Results in extensive protein depletion leading to muscle wasting, weakness, carbohydrate intolerance resulting in possible DM

slides.title: Cushing's Disease
text: Assist with care or give complete care
Report sore throat and low-grade fever

slides.title: The nurse is assessing a client who has possible Cushing’s syndrome.  The nurse expects to find:
text: The nurse is assessing a client who has possible Cushing’s syndrome.  The nurse expects to find:
weight gain in arms and legs.

slides.title: Addison's Disease
text: Caused by adrenalectomy or sudden withdrawal from from corticosteroids
May Lead to Adrenal Crisis (Addisonian Crisis)
Caused by extreme stress, salt deprivation, infection, cold exposure, excessive sweating

slides.title: Addison's Crisis
text: Always carry an emergency syringe of hydrocortisone
Increase corticosteroids to meet the demand
Keep environment warm and stress free
DEATH may result from hypotension and vasomotor collapse

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Practice Question
text: The nurse is teaching a client who has diabetes mellitus (type 2) and a prescription for extended-release metformin. Select 2 statements the nurse should make.
“You may chew the tablet if you experience any difficulty swallowing.”
“You need to carry emergency identification and a glucagon kit at all times.”
“You should contact the physician if you notice the metformin tablet in the stool.”
“You will need to discontinue the medication for any procedure that requires a contrast agent.”
